summary: Weert (Limburg) charges for parking in and around its centre. Street parking in zones 1 and 2 is paid Monday to Saturday 09:00-18:00, zone 3 is a permit-only area, and six municipal garages plus the surface lot Centrum-Noord charge 24 hours a day. Under the 2026 tariff table (council decision of 16 December 2025, levy from 1 January 2026) the rate is 1.70 euros per hour and 6.60 euros per day in the garages and on the street, unchanged from the 2025 ordinance, and the enforcement surcharge is 82.00 euros. A 24/7 garage subscription costs 600 euros a year, a Centrum-Noord subscription 313.90 euros, and a resident street permit 156.95 euros in zones 1 and 2 and 40.15 euros in zone 3. The 500-hour employee parking bundle (100 euros) is temporarily unavailable for three busy garages (Centrumgarage, Walburgpassage and Poort van Limburg) because of high parking pressure. The garages list 22 electric charge points in total. The P+R lot at Parallelweg by the station is run by Q-Park, is not managed by the municipality and has its own tariffs (295 spaces according to Q-Park). The municipality announced that street card readers for the Weerterlandpas and Stadsparkeren card stop working from 1 October 2026 because 2G is being phased out. The station area is the subject of a draft Spoorzone vision: at a meeting on 5 October 2026 the municipality showed a possible car-free station square, a new southern entrance and a car tunnel, which it says are not decisions. The council papers behind the 2025 parking standards note could not be opened because the council site was offline, so their content and adoption are not confirmed, and the old Centrum-Noord price of 298.50 euros still shown on one municipal page is the 2025 price.

items.text: The council adopted the 2026 parking tax ordinance on 16 December 2025 (published 19 December 2025, effective 1 January 2026). Garages and the Centrum-Noord lot charge 0.17 euros per 6 minutes, 1.70 euros per hour and 6.60 euros per day, 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.
items.source_title: Verordening parkeerbelastingen gemeente Weert 2026 (Gemeenteblad 2025, 558275) with Tarieventabel 2026

items.text: Street parking in zone 1 and zone 2 has the same rates (1.70 euros per hour, 6.60 euros per day) and is charged Monday to Saturday 09:00-18:00; some streets (for example Beekstraat, Korenmarkt, Hegstraat, Emmasingel, the Dries strip) have a 2-hour maximum and no day rate. The enforcement surcharge (naheffingsaanslag) is 82.00 euros in 2026, up from 78.80 euros in 2025.
items.source_title: Verordening parkeerbelastingen gemeente Weert 2026 (Gemeenteblad 2025, 558275) with Tarieventabel 2026

items.text: The 2025 parking tax ordinance, adopted on 18 December 2024 (published 23 December 2024, levy from 1 January 2025), set garage and street tariffs at 1.70 euros per hour and 6.60 euros per day, with an enforcement surcharge of 78.80 euros (76.70 in 2024).

The 2026 tariff table lists a 24/7 garage subscription at 600 euros per year (Centrumgarage, Poort van Limburg, Stationspleingarage, Muntgarage, Ursulinengarage, Walburgpassage), an OV-traveller subscription for Stationspleingarage or Centrumgarage at 504 euros, and a Centrum-Noord lot subscription raised from 298.50 to 313.90 euros. Resident street permits cost 156.95 euros per year in zones 1 and 2 and 40.15 euros in zone 3.
items.source_title: Verordening parkeerbelastingen gemeente Weert 2026 (Gemeenteblad 2025, 558275) with Tarieventabel 2026

items.text: The digital visitor scheme for zone 3 is priced in the 2026 tariff table at 0.15 euros per hour for residents' visitors and 0.30 euros per hour for businesses.
items.source_title: Verordening parkeerbelastingen gemeente Weert 2026 (Gemeenteblad 2025, 558275) with Tarieventabel 2026

items.text: The municipal designation decision (Aanwijzingsbesluit betaald parkeren 2023, effective 20 June 2023, published 30 June 2023) sets paid street parking in zones 1 and 2 for Monday to Saturday 09:00-18:00 and names seven pay-after-parking sites open round the clock: Centrumgarage, Walburgpassage, Ursulinengarage, Poort van Limburg, Stationspleingarage, Muntgarage and the lot Centrum-Noord. Permit-only zone 3 covers about 66 streets, among them Parallelweg, Spoorstraat, Maaseikerweg and Suffolkweg.

The 2023 designation decision sets zone 3 permit hours at Monday to Saturday 09:00-18:00 with Thursday until 20:00 (until 21:00 near the hospital for 09:00-20:00 streets); the 2026 tariff table words these hours slightly differently (18:00 or 20:00, Thursday until 21:00), so the exact current hours should be checked.

The municipal parking page (read on 21 October 2026) says paid street parking applies Monday to Saturday 09:00-18:00 and that no payment is needed on the street on shopping evenings (Thursday evening), (shopping) Sundays and official public holidays. Disabled badge holders may park free for up to 3 hours, with a parking disc, on general disabled bays on the street in the centre; this does not apply in garages or other parking places. Garages and lots with a barrier charge 24 hours a day.

Page read on 21 October 2026: residents in zones 1 and 2 may receive at most 2 street permits per address and in zone 3 at most 3, minus any private parking space or driveway; for some addresses in the centre no street permit is issued under agreements in the building permit. Employees working in zone 1 and 2 businesses can only get a zone 2 street permit, and the municipality says residents cannot expect to park in front of their door.
items.source_title: Parkeervergunning bewoners (op straat parkeren) and Parkeren - Gemeente Weert

items.text: The municipal parking page (read on 21 October 2026) lists six car parks in the centre (Centrumgarage under the town hall, Walburgpassage, Ursulinengarage, Poort van Limburg, Stationspleingarage, Muntgarage) and the Centrum-Noord lot, all charged at the municipal rates. It lists the P+R lot at Parallelweg as 'Q-Park', says it is not managed by the municipality and has its own tariffs.

Q-Park's page for P+R Parallelweg (6001 HM Weert, read on 21 October 2026) shows 295 parking spaces (4 for disabled users), a 2.10 m clearance, opening 24 hours a day on all days, licence-plate recognition and an NS rail-traveller discount for same-day domestic train journeys, with subscription options; the tariff table did not load when read.
items.source_title: Parkeren bij Q-Park P+R Parallelweg - Q-Park Weert

items.text: In April 2021 the municipality published a European open tender for the digital issue of parking products (permits, subscriptions, bundles), with the contract planned to start on 1 September 2021. A memo attached to the tender describing the processes at that time says that bundle applications and garage subscriptions were created manually in Parkbase, a system of IP Parking, and that a link to that system was not required. The memo does not say who won the tender, and the arrangement may have changed since 2021.
items.source_title: Digitale uitgifte parkeerproducten Weert (TenderNed 226166) and attached memo

items.text: Page read on 21 October 2026: the 500-hour employee parking bundle (100 euros, 0.20 euros per hour, valid one year) is temporarily unavailable for Centrumgarage, Walburgpassage and Poort van Limburg because of high parking pressure, and Poort van Limburg shows a waiting list. The bundle is still offered for Stationspleingarage, Muntgarage, Ursulinengarage and Centrum-Noord.

The municipal parking map (read on 21 October 2026) lists public charge points inside the car parks: Centrumgarage 10, Ursulinengarage 4, Walburgpassage 4, Poort van Limburg 2 and Muntgarage 2, with none listed for Stationspleingarage; opening hours are 24/7 except Ursulinengarage (06:00-23:00 entry) and clearances are 1.90-2.10 m.

The municipality announced on 10 August 2026 that the Weerterlandpas and Stadsparkeren card readers for street parking stop working from 1 October 2026 because the 2G network is being phased out nationally. The Stadsparkeren app remains usable and nothing changes for other parkers.
items.source_title: Paslezers voor straatparkeren verdwijnen per 1 oktober 2026 - Gemeente Weert

items.text: The garages use licence-plate recognition for subscribers with a pass as fallback, and some street machines and the Stationspleingarage and Poort van Limburg accept card payment only; the municipal page lists cash, debit card, credit card and pay-later by phone.
items.source_title: Parkeermogelijkheden en tarieven - Gemeente Weert; Parkeerabonnement (parkeergarage of -terrein)

items.text: At a public meeting on 5 October 2026 (33 participants) on the station area, the municipality presented a first future picture with a possible car-free station square, a new southern station entrance and a tunnel for car traffic; the report says these are not decisions. A concept vision slide adds cars and bicycles parking on the embankment along the railway.
items.source_title: Inloopavond stationsgebied levert waardevolle input op; Verslag en presentatie 5 oktober 2026 (Spoorzone)

items.text: The second Spoorzone festival on 5 March 2026 (120 participants) presented a concept area vision; recorded resident comments include difficulty imagining 'parking in hubs' and worry about where cars will park with many new homes. The municipal page then expected the council to discuss the vision in May or June 2026; the outcome was not found.
items.source_title: Spoorzone - Gemeente Weert; Beeldverslag Tweede Spoorzone Festival

items.text: Page read on 21 October 2026: permits, subscriptions and bundles are requested and managed through a digital parking desk, and the municipal page names the ParkerenPlus app for mobile payment in Weert; the August 2026 notice names the Stadsparkeren app.

gaps: Council site gemeenteraad.weert.nl returned HTTP 503 ('omgevingen tijdelijk offline', PHP precaution) on 21 October 2026, so none of these could be read: Raadsvoorstel Parkeerkaders en Nota Parkeernormen (https://gemeenteraad.weert.nl/Vergaderingen/Raadscommissie-Ruimte-en-Economie/2025/30-oktober/19:30/Parkeerkaders-en-nota-parkeernormen/Raadsvoorstel-Parkeerkaders-en-Nota-Parkeernormen-Weert.pdf), Bijlage 1 Parkeerkaders and Bijlage 2 Nota Parkeernormen, the VVD questions of 26 March 2025, the motion on smart parking systems of 9 April 2025, and the Raadsvoorstel Belastingverordeningen en tarieven 2026. Adoption of the parking framework and any parking guidance decision are therefore unconfirmed.
Q-Park P+R Parallelweg: tariffs and space count did not load on https://www.q-park.nl/nl-nl/parkeren/weert/p-r-parallelweg/; no independent source on its occupancy found.

No readable regional press (De Limburger, L1, Weert24, Hart van Limburg) on Weert parking was found or opened; no utilisation statistics, parking guidance (PGS) or open-data feed for the city centre was found.

The Spoorzone concept presentation of 5 March 2026 (https://www.weert.nl/Downloads/Spoorzone/Spoorzone%20-%2004%20Festival%202%20Presentatie%20concept%20gebiedsvisie%2005-03-2026.pdf) is image-only and was not readable; the council outcome on the vision (May/June 2026) was not found.
weert.nl/parkeerabonnement-parkeergarage-of-terrein still shows the old Centrum-Noord subscription price of 298.50 euros; the 2026 tariff table (313.90) was used.
